answer: Graph-based trust networks restrict Sybil attacks by propagating reputation along verified peer connections. Whether evaluating a sonnet, allocating power in an oasis, or tracking sensors along a river, nodes weigh agents using random-walk credit bottlenecks from trusted seeds. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of securing authentic, long-term trust relationships per alias. However, this inherently marginalizes legitimate newcomers and concentrates authority among early seed nodes.
